speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. Since you are a newborn, I will rely on your caregiver for your history and symptoms; have you noticed any discoloration of your skin, particularly on the trunk or extremities?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for providing that history; the lack of prenatal care and immunizations is a significant concern. Given the newborn status, have you noticed any jaundice, lethargy, poor feeding, or signs of infection such as fever or temperature instability?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Congenital Rubella Syndrome.

The combination of a continuous heart murmur (likely Patent Ductus Arteriosus), bluish non-blanching macules (blueberry muffin rash), cataracts, and deafness is the classic tetrad of this condition. Given the lack of prenatal care and immunizations, is there any history of rubella infection in the mother during the first trimester?
